Work in C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod (a Next.js 16 + Prisma app called Kodely — an AI website builder).

BUILD: the project-management operations the dashboard is missing — rename, duplicate, and delete a site.

## Why
Users can create projects and open them, but cannot rename, duplicate, or delete one. Delete is the sharpest gap: there is no way to get rid of a bad first attempt, so dashboards fill with junk and there is no way to withdraw a published site. Duplicate matters because "make a variant of this" currently means paying for a whole new generation.

## Scope — YOU MAY ONLY EDIT `app/api/projects/[id]/route.ts` AND FILES UNDER `app/dashboard/`
You may CREATE new files under `app/dashboard/`. Everything else is off limits — other agents are working in parallel. Read anything you need to understand the system.

## What to build
1. **Rename** — PATCH on `app/api/projects/[id]/route.ts`. Name only. Trim, cap length (the create route caps at 80 — match it). Decide deliberately whether the slug changes and JUSTIFY it in a comment: the slug is the published URL (`<slug>.kodely.site`), so changing it on rename would break every existing link to a published site. Think hard about the right answer here.

2. **Duplicate** — a copy of the project: its name (something like "X (copy)"), a NEW unique slug, all draft source files, and NOT the published state (a copy must not silently go live at a new URL) and NOT the message history or build history. Charges no credits — nothing is generated. Read `app/api/projects/route.ts` to see how slugs are made and how files are created.

3. **Delete** — DELETE on the same route. Ownership-scoped. Note that Prisma `onDelete: Cascade` already handles files/messages/builds — check prisma/schema.prisma (READ ONLY) to confirm before relying on it, and confirm what happens to CreditLedger rows referencing deleted builds (there is a `SetNull` in there — verify). **Deleting a published site must take it offline.** Requires a confirmation step in the UI — type-the-name or an explicit two-step, not a bare `confirm()`. This is irreversible and there is no undo, so the UI must make that plain.

4. **Dashboard UI** — a per-project menu on each row in `app/dashboard/page.tsx` (currently each project is a plain `<Link>`). Keep the existing visual idiom exactly: `rounded-xl border border-black/10 dark:border-white/10`, `text-sm`, restrained monochrome, no new colours except semantic red for delete. Keyboard accessible, visible focus state.

## Critical constraints
- **Ownership scoping is the security-critical part.** Every operation must scope by `userId` IN THE SAME QUERY as the id (the existing code does `findFirst({ where: { id, userId: user.id } })`) so a wrong-user id is indistinguishable from a nonexistent one. Never trust the route param alone. Read the existing GET handler in that file and match its auth idiom.
- DO NOT modify: prisma/schema.prisma, lib/credits.ts, lib/agent.ts, lib/agent-sdk.ts, lib/build-site.ts, lib/events.ts, lib/build-narration.ts, lib/auth.ts, app/api/projects/route.ts, app/api/generate/route.ts, app/api/projects/[id]/publish/route.ts, app/api/projects/[id]/export/route.ts, app/projects/**, app/settings/**, app/globals.css, proxy.ts, deploy.sh, .env, package.json.
- NOTE: `app/dashboard/page.tsx` was just modified — it now imports and renders a `CreditMeter` component and a Settings link. Read it fresh before editing and preserve those.
- DO NOT add npm dependencies.
- DO NOT run `npm run build`, `git commit`, `git push`, or `deploy.sh`.
- Run `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx eslint <your files>`; your files must be clean. Pre-existing errors elsewhere (PromptHero.tsx, ThemeToggle.tsx and others have some) are NOT yours — leave them.
- You may test against the local Postgres (DATABASE_URL is in .env) but do NOT delete data you did not create.

## Report back
What you built, your slug-on-rename decision and the reasoning, what cascade behaviour you actually verified vs assumed, and how you tested.

content.text:
Clean. My changes are confined to the three files in scope (the other modified files belong to the parallel agents).

## What I built

**`app/api/projects/[id]/route.ts`** — added `PATCH` (rename) and `POST` (duplicate), documented the pre-existing `DELETE`, left `GET` untouched.

- **Rename (PATCH)** — name only. Trim → cap at 80 (matching the create route) → trim again, since slicing at 80 can leave a trailing space. Rejects empty/whitespace/non-string/malformed-JSON with 400. Deliberately does *not* fall back to `"Untitled site"` the way the create route does: silently renaming someone's site to a placeholder because their input was blank is worse than refusing.
- **Duplicate (POST)** — copies name (`X (copy)`) and all draft files; new unique slug; no publish state, no messages, no builds; charges nothing.
- **Delete (DELETE)** — already existed and was already correctly scoped; I verified its cascade behaviour and documented it rather than rewriting it.

**`app/dashboard/ProjectRow.tsx`** (new) + a small edit to `app/dashboard/page.tsx` to render it. `CreditMeter`, the Settings link, and `TopUpButton` are preserved untouched.

## Slug-on-rename decision: the slug never changes

`slug` is the published address and the key the public site route resolves by. Re-slugging on rename would (a) 404 every existing inbound link, share and search result with no redirect to fall back on, and (b) release a globally-unique slug back into the pool, so someone else could later claim the exact URL the user just vacated — a URL takeover triggered by an action that looks purely cosmetic.

I also kept it unconditional rather than "re-slug only while it's still a draft". A conditional rule means the dashboard slug silently changes for a draft then freezes at publish — unpredictable from the UI, and it breaks preview URLs the user may already have shared. One rule: a slug is assigned once at creation and never moves. The UI states this inline during rename ("The address stays `<slug>` — renaming never changes a site's URL"), and a user who genuinely wants a different address gets one from Duplicate.

## Cascade behaviour — verified, not assumed

Queried the live Postgres `pg_constraint` catalog directly, then confirmed each one empirically by deleting a fully-populated project:

| FK | Rule | Verified outcome |
|---|---|---|
| `ProjectFile → Project` | CASCADE | all rows gone, draft **and** published |
| `Message → Project` | CASCADE | gone |
| `Build → Project` | CASCADE | gone |
| `CreditLedger → Build` | **SET NULL** | **row survives**, `buildId` becomes null |

Two things I confirmed rather than trusted:

1. **Deleting a published site takes it offline.** The cascade removes the `published: true` rows *and* the Project row the slug resolves by — `GET /api/site/<slug>` went 200 → 404 across the delete. One caveat I could not fix in scope: that route sends `Cache-Control: public, max-age=60`, so a cached response can survive up to a minute at the edge/browser after deletion.
2. **The credit ledger is untouched.** `getBalance` reads `balanceAfter` off the newest ledger row, and those rows survive with `buildId: null` — balance was identical before and after (738 → 738). Deleting the artifact does not un-charge the work, which is correct for an auditable ledger.

## Ownership scoping

Every operation scopes by `userId` in the *same* query as the id. For rename I used `updateMany`, not `update` — `update` can only filter on unique fields, so it would have to take the id alone and check ownership in a second query. Verified with a second user: PATCH, POST and DELETE against another user's project all return `404 "Project not found."`, identical to a nonexistent id, with no state change and nothing duplicated into the attacker's account.

## UI

Per-row `···` menu → Rename / Duplicate / Delete. Rename edits inline in the row; duplicate is one click; delete opens a modal. Existing idiom kept exactly (`rounded-xl border border-black/10 dark:border-white/10`, `text-sm`, monochrome, red only on delete). Keyboard: arrow/Home/End roving focus, Escape closes and restores focus to the trigger, Tab closes, `aria-haspopup`/`aria-expanded`/`role="menu"`, and a visible `focus-visible:ring-2` on every control.

**Delete confirmation is graded by stakes** — both forms the brief sanctioned:
- **Published** → must type the exact site name, plus an explicit warning that `<slug>.kodely.site` goes offline immediately and the address cannot be reclaimed.
- **Draft** → explicit two-step (menu → dialog → Delete).

The reasoning: the brief frames delete as the fix for dashboards full of junk first attempts, and a name-typing gate on every throwaway draft just trains people to type it without reading. Both variants state plainly that it cannot be undone, and note that credit history is unaffected.

## One judgement call worth flagging

The brief said duplicate should copy "all draft source files". I copy **all draft files, both kinds** (`source` and `build`). The editor preview reads draft `kind: "build"` rows — copying only source would hand the user a duplicate that renders "Nothing built yet" and force a paid rebuild to see it, which is exactly the cost this feature exists to avoid. Published rows are still excluded, so the copy cannot go live. Reasoning is in a comment on the handler.

Also: `EVENTS` in `lib/events.ts` is a deliberately closed vocabulary and that file is off limits, so duplicate tracks as `projectCreated` with `source: "duplicate"` rather than inventing a name. **Delete is currently untracked** — there is no suitable event name and I could not add one; worth a follow-up edit to `lib/events.ts` by whoever owns it.

## Testing

- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean (repo baseline was already clean). `npx eslint` on all three files — clean.
- **45-assertion end-to-end script** against the running dev server and the local Postgres, covering cross-user scoping, unauthenticated 401s, rename trimming/capping/validation, slug and `publishedAt` stability, the full duplicate shape, live-site-before/404-after, and every cascade row above. All 45 passed.
- **Browser-driven UI test**: menu open/arrow-nav/Escape/focus-return, both delete-dialog variants (verified the Delete button stays disabled until the typed name matches exactly), and a real rename, duplicate and delete each confirmed in the database.
- All test data was created by me and has been removed; I deleted nothing I did not create.
